newsitem.title: USA: Market Hub gets FERC Clearance for Egan expansion.
newsitem.headline: Market Hub gets FERC Clearance for Egan expansion.

text.p: Market Hub Partners LP said Friday its subsidiary, Egan Hub Partners LP, has received a certificate of public convenience and necessity from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for the Egan natural gas storage facility.

This certificate grants Market Hub authority to operate its existing facilities and to build a second salt cavern storage facility at the Egan hub capable of serving customers via a recently completed interconnection with Columbia Gas System Inc's Columbia Gulf Transmission Company.

With FERC's approval, "we are ready to undertake the expansion of our Egan facility," said Market Hub, pointing out "Egan is the first hub facility in the United States with FERC authorization to charge market-based rates."
Market Hub is owned by TPC Corp, NIPSCO Industries Inc, New Jersey Resources Corp, Miami Valley Leasing Inc and Public Service Enterprise Group Inc.

The partnership is developing a system of natural gas market centers with high-deliverability salt cavern storage facilities that include the Moss Bluff facility in Texas, the Egan facility in Louisiana and three other market hubs which are in various stages of development at locations in Mississippi, Pennsylvania and in the Midwest.

The Egan facility is located on the Jennings Salt Dome in Acadia Parish, La. Construction of the first cavern began in early 1994 and operations commenced September 1, 1995, with 4.5 billion cubic feet of natural gas storage capacity, 135 million cubic feet per day of injection capacity and 750 million cubic feet of daily withdrawal capacity.
Construction of the second phase, a single cavern with natural gas storage capacity of some 4.0 Billion cubic feet, will begin shortly, it said. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
